302	// run is one coloured stretch of an already-fitted cell.
303	type run struct {
304		text  string
305		style lipgloss.Style
306	}
307	
308	// multiRunCell renders a cell that colours more than one stretch of its text:
309	// Column.Spans when it answers a non-empty list, else Cut/TailStyle. ok is false
310	// for an ordinary one-run cell, which the caller renders through cellStyle.
311	func (m *Model[T]) multiRunCell(c Column[T], item T, fitted string, selected bool) (string, bool) {
312		if c.Spans != nil {
313			if spans := c.Spans(item); len(spans) > 0 {
314				return m.renderRuns(m.spanRuns(c, item, spans, fitted, selected)), true
315			}
316			return "", false
317		}
318		if c.TailStyle == nil {
319			return "", false
320		}
321		return m.splitCellRun(c, item, fitted, selected), true
322	}
323	
324	// spanRuns lays spans over the fitted text from left to right: a negative width
325	// counts as 0, a zero-width span yields no run, what overflows the cell is cut
326	// and the cells left after the last span take c.Style. Widths are in runes, so
327	// like Cut they assume single-width glyphs.
328	func (m *Model[T]) spanRuns(c Column[T], item T, spans []Span, fitted string, selected bool) []run {
329		runes := []rune(fitted)
330		var runs []run
331		pos := 0
332		for _, s := range spans {
333			end := min(pos+max(s.Width, 0), len(runes))
334			if end > pos {
335				runs = append(runs, run{string(runes[pos:end]), m.runStyle(s.Style, selected)})
336				pos = end
337			}
338		}
339		if pos < len(runes) {
340			runs = append(runs, run{string(runes[pos:]), m.runStyle(m.styleOf(c.Style, item), selected)})
341		}
342		return runs
343	}
344	
345	// splitCellRun renders a two-colour cell: c.Style covers the first c.Cut(item)
346	// cells of the already-fitted text, c.TailStyle the rest, as two runs.
347	//
348	// fitted is exactly cols[i].Width runes (fit() guarantees it), so slicing by
349	// rune index is safe: every glyph a caller uses here — braille, ASCII, the
350	// truncation marker — is single-width, which callers are expected to keep
351	// true rather than this function verifying it.
352	//
353	// selected mirrors cellStyle's own selected branch: on the plain "normal"
354	// selection (m.preserveColumnColors), both runs repaint ColorTableLineSelected and
355	// bold themselves instead of each keeping their unselected background — the
356	// same per-cell repaint that makes a single-run selected cell safe applies
357	// unchanged to two runs, since a reset between them only ever uncovers that
358	// same shared background, immediately repainted by the run that follows.
359	// This is what lets a load gauge (Cut/TailStyle) keep its fill/track split
360	// under the cursor instead of collapsing to Style's fill colour alone.
361	func (m *Model[T]) splitCellRun(c Column[T], item T, fitted string, selected bool) string {
362		runes := []rune(fitted)
363		cut := min(max(c.Cut(item), 0), len(runes))
364		return m.renderRuns([]run{
365			{string(runes[:cut]), m.runStyle(m.styleOf(c.Style, item), selected)},
366			{string(runes[cut:]), m.runStyle(m.styleOf(c.TailStyle, item), selected)},
367		})
368	}
369	
370	// renderRuns renders the runs of one cell side by side. The column's 1-cell
371	// padding goes on the outer edge of the first and last run as literal spaces
372	// rather than lipgloss's Padding property, so runs don't each add their own pair
373	// and open a gap at a boundary. Every run given is rendered, empty or not:
374	// callers that must not emit an empty styled run drop it beforehand.
375	func (m *Model[T]) renderRuns(runs []run) string {
376		var b strings.Builder
377		for i, r := range runs {
378			text := r.text
379			if i == 0 {
380				text = " " + text
381			}
382			if i == len(runs)-1 {
383				text += " "
384			}
385			b.WriteString(r.style.Render(text))
386		}
387		return b.String()
388	}
389	
390	// styleOf evaluates an optional per-item style function; nil gives the zero style.
391	func (m *Model[T]) styleOf(fn func(T) lipgloss.Style, item T) lipgloss.Style {
392		if fn == nil {
393			return lipgloss.NewStyle()
394		}
395		return fn(item)
396	}

398	// runStyle applies the same foreground/background defaulting cellStyle gives
399	// a single-run cell, minus the Padding — renderRuns already pads with
400	// literal characters — so a multi-run cell is indistinguishable from a one-run
401	// one everywhere but the run boundaries.
402	//
403	// selected forces the shared selection background and bold weight
404	// unconditionally, exactly as cellStyle's selected branch does for a
405	// single-run cell — unlike the unselected path below, this overrides
406	// whatever background the run's own style already set (GaugeTrackStyle
407	// sets one explicitly), because the selected row's background is the
408	// highlight itself, not a fallback for an unset one.
409	func (m *Model[T]) runStyle(style lipgloss.Style, selected bool) lipgloss.Style {
410		if _, unset := style.GetForeground().(lipgloss.NoColor); unset {
411			style = style.Foreground(theme.ColorText)
412		}
413		if selected {
414			return style.Background(theme.ColorTableLineSelected).Bold(true)
415		}
416		if _, unset := style.GetBackground().(lipgloss.NoColor); unset {
417			style = style.Background(theme.ColorBackground)
418		}
419		return style
420	}

422	// clampOffset moves the scroll window the least it can to keep the cursor in
423	// it. bubbles kept this in an unexported viewport; owning the rendering means
424	// owning the offset too.
425	//
426	// The window is only moved when the cursor has left it, so a reload that keeps
427	// the cursor on screen keeps the scroll position — the property SetItems was
428	// written to protect.
429	func (m *Model[T]) clampOffset() {
430		height := max(m.table.Height(), 1)
431		last := max(len(m.visible)-height, 0)
432	
433		m.offset = min(max(m.offset, 0), last)
434	
435		switch cursor := m.table.Cursor(); {
436		case cursor < 0: // nothing selected: an empty table scrolls nowhere
437			m.offset = 0
438		case cursor < m.offset:
439			m.offset = cursor
440		case cursor >= m.offset+height:
441			m.offset = cursor - height + 1
442		}
443	}

445	// Offset reports the first visible row, for tests that check the window
446	// follows the cursor without going through the rendered string.
447	func (m *Model[T]) Offset() int { return m.offset }

14	// Why this package renders its own rows rather than calling table.Model.View().
15	//
16	// bubbles/table builds a cell as:
17	//
18	//	m.styles.Cell.Render(style.Render(runewidth.Truncate(value, width, "…")))
19	//
20	// — it measures the value *before* styling it, with runewidth, which counts an
21	// escape sequence's bytes as width. A seven-cell string carrying a colour
22	// measures 28, so it is truncated in a column twice wide enough, and the cut
23	// lands inside the escape: "\x1b[38;2;166;2…". The unterminated sequence then
24	// bleeds over every row below. That is Rule 122, and no configuration of
25	// bubbles avoids it — bubbles v1.0.0 has the same line.
26	//
27	// Here the order is inverted: Cell returns plain text, which is what gets
28	// measured and truncated, and Style is applied to the finished cell. Nothing
29	// styled is ever measured, so the failure is unexpressible rather than
30	// forbidden by review.
31	//
32	// The other half of the reason is the selected row. bubbles hands the whole
33	// joined row to styles.Selected, and a colour inside it closes with a reset
34	// that takes the selection background with it for the rest of the line — the
35	// highlight ends mid-row. A row a view has coloured whole (error, busy, a CVE
36	// severity) still drops per-cell colours for exactly that reason (see
37	// cellStyle). The plain "normal" selection instead gives every cell the
38	// *same* background itself, which sidesteps the defect rather than reproduces
39	// it — a reset between two cells never uncovers anything but that shared
40	// background again.

42	// truncationMarker ends a cell too narrow for its content.
43	const truncationMarker = "…"

45	// View renders the header and the window of rows around the cursor.
46	func (m *Model[T]) View() string {
47		cols := m.table.Columns()
48		// At least one line under the header. A terminal too short to hold a single
49		// row leaves Height() at 0, and a table that renders literally nothing
50		// closes the viewport border onto itself — bubbles' viewport always emitted
51		// that line, and two views check for it at 20x1.
52		rows := max(m.table.Height(), 1)
53	
54		lines := make([]string, 0, rows+1)
55		lines = append(lines, m.headerLine(cols))
56	
57		cursor := m.table.Cursor()
58		for i := m.offset; i < len(m.visible) && len(lines) <= rows; i++ {
59			lines = append(lines, m.rowLine(cols, m.visible[i], i == cursor))
60		}
61		// Pad to the full height so the viewport border does not close in on a
62		// short list. bubbles' viewport did this with unstyled lines; filling them
63		// with the app background is Rule 115 applied to the one part of the table
64		// that had escaped it.
65		blank := theme.EmptyLineBg(contentWidth(cols))
66		for len(lines) <= rows {
67			lines = append(lines, blank)
68		}
69		return strings.Join(lines, "\n")
70	}

72	// RenderedWidth is what the table's lines actually span. It equals the viewport
73	// interior — the width passed to Resize, less its two borders — whenever
74	// Rule 116 holds, and it is what a view's layout test should assert on.
75	//
76	// Summing the declared columns' widths and adding two per column is the
77	// tempting version, and it is what every one of those tests did. It is wrong as
78	// soon as a column is dropped for want of room: the dropped column renders
79	// nothing and its padding goes back into the budget, so the formula asks for
80	// less than the line spans and fails on a layout that is correct. That
81	// disagreement was D61 seen from the other side.
82	func (m *Model[T]) RenderedWidth() int { return contentWidth(m.table.Columns()) }
83	
84	// contentWidth is what the rendered lines span: every column plus the padding
85	// bubbles adds around each. It equals the viewport width less its two borders
86	// whenever Rule 116 holds, but it is measured rather than assumed so that a
87	// table that has never been resized still pads to its own content.
88	func contentWidth(cols []table.Column) int {
89		width := 0
90		for _, col := range cols {
91			if col.Width > 0 {
92				width += col.Width + cellPadding
93			}
94		}
95		return width
96	}

102			if col.Width <= 0 {
103				continue
104			}
105			// A header is cut at its end whatever the column asks for its values: a
106			// title is recognised by how it starts, and TruncateHead is a statement
107			// about the data.
108			line.WriteString(m.styles.Header.Render(fit(col.Title, col.Width, false)))
109		}

113	// rowLine renders one row.
114	//
115	// A busy row shows its activity glyph in the Indicator column instead of that
116	// column's own cell — on the selected row too. The glyph is the primary signal,
117	// and a signal that disappears under the cursor is one the user loses exactly
118	// when they are looking at it.
119	func (m *Model[T]) rowLine(cols []table.Column, item T, selected bool) string {
120		_, busy := m.busyLabel(item)
121	
122		var line strings.Builder
123		for i, c := range m.cfg.Columns {
124			if i >= len(cols) || cols[i].Width <= 0 {
125				continue
126			}
127			state := indicator.Idle
128			if c.Indicator != nil {
129				state = m.indicatorState(c, item, busy)
130			}
131			text := c.Cell(item)
132			if state != indicator.Idle {
133				text = indicator.Glyph(state, m.blinkOn)
134				// Padded with runewidth, not lipgloss: lipgloss always counts an
135				// ambiguous-width glyph as one cell, runewidth follows the terminal.
136				fitted := runewidth.FillRight(text, cols[i].Width)
137				line.WriteString(m.indicatorCellStyle(state, selected).Render(fitted))
138				continue
139			}
140			fitted := fit(text, cols[i].Width, c.TruncateHead)
141			if !busy && (!selected || m.preserveColumnColors) {
142				if runs, ok := m.multiRunCell(c, item, fitted, selected); ok {
143					line.WriteString(runs)
144					continue
145				}
146			}
147			line.WriteString(m.cellStyle(c, item, selected, busy).Render(fitted))
148		}
149		if selected {
150			return m.styles.Selected.Render(m.padToContent(line.String()))
151		}
152		return line.String()
153	}

241	// **The plain "normal" selection is the opposite case** (§3.72 in the
242	// backlog, m.preserveColumnColors): each cell keeps its own colour and
243	// additionally repaints ColorTableLineSelected and bold **itself**, rather than
244	// once on an outer wrap. That is what makes it safe rather than a return of
245	// the defect above — every cell's own reset only ever uncovers the *same*
246	// background the next cell immediately repaints, so nothing but that
247	// background is ever exposed between two cells. styles.Selected still wraps
248	// the joined line afterward (rowLine), painting the same background again;
249	// by then it is redundant colour, not load-bearing, and it is what still
250	// pads the row out to the full content width.
251	//
252	// Off the selected row every cell carries an explicit foreground **and**
253	// background, whether or not the column asked for either. Both halves are
254	// forced for the same reason and each fixes its own defect:
255	//
256	//   - Background: lipgloss does not inherit one (Rule 115), and the app's
257	//     viewport style only reaches the cells that emit nothing of their own. One
258	//     coloured cell would otherwise end its line with a reset and strip the
259	//     background from everything to its right.
260	//   - Foreground: neither theme.DefaultTableStyles() nor bubbles' own sets one
261	//     on Cell, so a column that declares no Style rendered in whatever
262	//     foreground the terminal happens to use — the theme had no say. Four views
263	//     had written `Foreground(theme.ColorText)` into a Style of their own to get
264	//     it back, which is the shape a missing default takes.
265	//
266	// The busy row, for its part, does not consult `Style` either: what it says
267	// is that an operation is in progress, and a color by severity or by state
268	// on top of that would say the opposite. Every cell goes to `DimStyle` — the
269	// displayed state is in the process of ceasing to be true; the activity glyph
270	// is drawn by the Indicator column.
271	func (m *Model[T]) cellStyle(c Column[T], item T, selected, busy bool) lipgloss.Style {
272		if selected {
273			if !m.preserveColumnColors {
274				// Neither background nor text here: they would hide those of styles.Selected.
275				return m.styles.Cell
276			}
277			style := m.styles.Cell
278			if c.Style != nil {
279				style = c.Style(item).Padding(0, 1)
280			}
281			if _, unset := style.GetForeground().(lipgloss.NoColor); unset {
282				style = style.Foreground(theme.ColorText)
283			}
284			return style.Background(theme.ColorTableLineSelected).Bold(true)
285		}
286		if busy {
287			return theme.DimStyle.Padding(0, 1).Background(theme.ColorBackground)
288		}
289		if c.Style == nil {
290			return m.styles.Cell.Foreground(theme.ColorText).Background(theme.ColorBackground)
291		}
292		style := c.Style(item).Padding(0, 1)
293		if _, unset := style.GetForeground().(lipgloss.NoColor); unset {
294			style = style.Foreground(theme.ColorText)
295		}
296		if _, unset := style.GetBackground().(lipgloss.NoColor); unset {
297			style = style.Background(theme.ColorBackground)
298		}
299		return style
300	}
301	
302	// run is one coloured stretch of an already-fitted cell.
303	type run struct {
304		text  string
305		style lipgloss.Style
306	}
307	
308	// multiRunCell renders a cell that colours more than one stretch of its text:
309	// Column.Spans when it answers a non-empty list, else Cut/TailStyle. ok is false
310	// for an ordinary one-run cell, which the caller renders through cellStyle.
311	func (m *Model[T]) multiRunCell(c Column[T], item T, fitted string, selected bool) (string, bool) {
312		if c.Spans != nil {
313			if spans := c.Spans(item); len(spans) > 0 {
314				return m.renderRuns(m.spanRuns(c, item, spans, fitted, selected)), true
315			}
316			return "", false
317		}
318		if c.TailStyle == nil {
319			return "", false
320		}
321		return m.splitCellRun(c, item, fitted, selected), true
322	}
323	
324	// spanRuns lays spans over the fitted text from left to right: a negative width
325	// counts as 0, a zero-width span yields no run, what overflows the cell is cut
326	// and the cells left after the last span take c.Style. Widths are in runes, so
327	// like Cut they assume single-width glyphs.
328	func (m *Model[T]) spanRuns(c Column[T], item T, spans []Span, fitted string, selected bool) []run {
329		runes := []rune(fitted)
330		var runs []run
331		pos := 0
332		for _, s := range spans {
333			end := min(pos+max(s.Width, 0), len(runes))
334			if end > pos {
335				runs = append(runs, run{string(runes[pos:end]), m.runStyle(s.Style, selected)})
336				pos = end
337			}
338		}
339		if pos < len(runes) {
340			runs = append(runs, run{string(runes[pos:]), m.runStyle(m.styleOf(c.Style, item), selected)})
341		}
342		return runs
343	}
344	
345	// splitCellRun renders a two-colour cell: c.Style covers the first c.Cut(item)
346	// cells of the already-fitted text, c.TailStyle the rest, as two runs.
347	//
348	// fitted is exactly cols[i].Width runes (fit() guarantees it), so slicing by
349	// rune index is safe: every glyph a caller uses here — braille, ASCII, the
350	// truncation marker — is single-width, which callers are expected to keep
351	// true rather than this function verifying it.
352	//
353	// selected mirrors cellStyle's own selected branch: on the plain "normal"
354	// selection (m.preserveColumnColors), both runs repaint ColorTableLineSelected and
355	// bold themselves instead of each keeping their unselected background — the
356	// same per-cell repaint that makes a single-run selected cell safe applies
357	// unchanged to two runs, since a reset between them only ever uncovers that
358	// same shared background, immediately repainted by the run that follows.
359	// This is what lets a load gauge (Cut/TailStyle) keep its fill/track split
360	// under the cursor instead of collapsing to Style's fill colour alone.
361	func (m *Model[T]) splitCellRun(c Column[T], item T, fitted string, selected bool) string {
362		runes := []rune(fitted)
363		cut := min(max(c.Cut(item), 0), len(runes))
364		return m.renderRuns([]run{
365			{string(runes[:cut]), m.runStyle(m.styleOf(c.Style, item), selected)},
366			{string(runes[cut:]), m.runStyle(m.styleOf(c.TailStyle, item), selected)},
367		})
368	}
369	
370	// renderRuns renders the runs of one cell side by side. The column's 1-cell
371	// padding goes on the outer edge of the first and last run as literal spaces
372	// rather than lipgloss's Padding property, so runs don't each add their own pair
373	// and open a gap at a boundary. Every run given is rendered, empty or not:
374	// callers that must not emit an empty styled run drop it beforehand.
375	func (m *Model[T]) renderRuns(runs []run) string {
376		var b strings.Builder
377		for i, r := range runs {
378			text := r.text
379			if i == 0 {
380				text = " " + text
381			}
382			if i == len(runs)-1 {
383				text += " "
384			}
385			b.WriteString(r.style.Render(text))
386		}
387		return b.String()
388	}
389	
390	// styleOf evaluates an optional per-item style function; nil gives the zero style.
391	func (m *Model[T]) styleOf(fn func(T) lipgloss.Style, item T) lipgloss.Style {
392		if fn == nil {
393			return lipgloss.NewStyle()
394		}
395		return fn(item)
396	}
397	
398	// runStyle applies the same foreground/background defaulting cellStyle gives
399	// a single-run cell, minus the Padding — renderRuns already pads with
400	// literal characters — so a multi-run cell is indistinguishable from a one-run
401	// one everywhere but the run boundaries.
402	//
403	// selected forces the shared selection background and bold weight
404	// unconditionally, exactly as cellStyle's selected branch does for a
405	// single-run cell — unlike the unselected path below, this overrides
406	// whatever background the run's own style already set (GaugeTrackStyle
407	// sets one explicitly), because the selected row's background is the
408	// highlight itself, not a fallback for an unset one.
409	func (m *Model[T]) runStyle(style lipgloss.Style, selected bool) lipgloss.Style {
410		if _, unset := style.GetForeground().(lipgloss.NoColor); unset {
411			style = style.Foreground(theme.ColorText)
412		}
413		if selected {
414			return style.Background(theme.ColorTableLineSelected).Bold(true)
415		}
416		if _, unset := style.GetBackground().(lipgloss.NoColor); unset {
417			style = style.Background(theme.ColorBackground)
418		}
419		return style
420	}
421	
422	// clampOffset moves the scroll window the least it can to keep the cursor in
423	// it. bubbles kept this in an unexported viewport; owning the rendering means
424	// owning the offset too.
425	//
426	// The window is only moved when the cursor has left it, so a reload that keeps
427	// the cursor on screen keeps the scroll position — the property SetItems was
428	// written to protect.
429	func (m *Model[T]) clampOffset() {
430		height := max(m.table.Height(), 1)
431		last := max(len(m.visible)-height, 0)
432	
433		m.offset = min(max(m.offset, 0), last)
434	
435		switch cursor := m.table.Cursor(); {
436		case cursor < 0: // nothing selected: an empty table scrolls nowhere
437			m.offset = 0
438		case cursor < m.offset:
439			m.offset = cursor
440		case cursor >= m.offset+height:
441			m.offset = cursor - height + 1
442		}
443	}
444	
445	// Offset reports the first visible row, for tests that check the window
446	// follows the cursor without going through the rendered string.
447	func (m *Model[T]) Offset() int { return m.offset }
448

280	`width(Title) + 2` for any column with a `Less` — otherwise a narrow one renders
281	`CRIT ▼` into five cells and loses exactly the character that says how it is
282	sorted. The reserve applies whether or not the column is the sorted one, so

file.content:
`width(Title) + 2` for any column with a `Less` — otherwise a narrow one renders
`CRIT ▼` into five cells and loses exactly the character that says how it is
sorted. The reserve applies whether or not the column is the sorted one, so
cycling `.` does not resize it and shift every column beside it.

**The package renders its own rows** (`render.go`), and that is what makes
`Style` possible at all. `bubbles/table` measures a cell with `runewidth`
*before* styling it, and runewidth counts an escape sequence's bytes as width: a
seven-cell string carrying a colour measures 28, so it is truncated in a column
twice wide enough and the cut lands inside the escape — the unterminated
sequence then bleeds over every row below. That is Rule 122, it is a
`bubbles/table` limitation rather than a Bubble Tea one, and Bubbles v2
(`charm.land/bubbles/v2`) has the same line. Inverting the order — `Cell` is measured while plain, `Style`
is applied to the finished cell — makes the failure unexpressible instead of
forbidden by review.

**Bubble Tea / Bubbles / Lip Gloss v2 (DEVDESK-201).** Components keep
`View() string`; only top-level views have `Render()` and a `View() tea.View`
(see `app-shell.md`). Colours are `color.Color`. Sizes go through accessors:
`textinput.SetWidth(n)` and `Width()`, `viewport.SetWidth/SetHeight` and
`Width()/Height()`, not field assignment. `lipgloss.Place` takes
`WithWhitespaceStyle(lipgloss.NewStyle().Background(theme.ColorBackground))`
(Rule 115). Two widths coexist: the table pads and cuts with `runewidth`,
Lip Gloss and the viewport measure with `x/ansi`; they differ on VS16 emoji
(Rule 116, pinned by `REDACTED`).

bubbles is still the state: rows, columns, cursor, focus and height. What moved
here is the drawing and the scroll offset (`clampOffset`), which its viewport
kept unexported. `Table()` reports the same thing it always did.

content.content:
555	  If several columns carry one, only the first is honoured (`indicatorAt`).
556	- **Precedence at render** (`indicatorState`, `render.go`): a row that is busy
557	  (`MarkBusy`) is `Running` whatever the column says; otherwise the column's
558	  own state. Busy still wins over the view's state, as in §3.22.
559	- The phase is **read at render**, so `SetBlinkPhase` rebuilds nothing, and a
560	  table never calls it in a test that wants the steady glyph.
561	- **Padding follows the terminal.** The glyphs `● ○ ◐ ◕ ◉` have ambiguous
562	  width. lipgloss always counts them as one cell; a terminal in East Asian mode
563	  draws two. An indicator cell is therefore padded with
564	  `runewidth.FillRight`, which follows `runewidth.DefaultCondition`.
565	- **The selected row is padded structurally**, not by measuring the rendered
566	  line: `padToContent` adds `gap = width - 2 - RenderedWidth()` spaces, computed
567	  from the column widths. A second measurement with another library would
568	  disagree on the same glyphs. `TestRule116HoldsUnderEastAsianWidth` pins it.
569	
570	- **`Shapes()` and `ActivityTable`** (`shape.go`, DEVDESK-142). A cross-view
571	  guard cannot call a generic `Model[T]` without knowing `T`, so
572	  `(*Model[T]).Shapes()` returns a fresh `[]ColumnShape` on each call
573	  (`Title`, `Sizing`, `MinWidth`, and whether the column declares
574	  `Indicator`, `Less`, `Search`). It reports the declared columns, in order,
575	  even for an empty table, and mutating the result changes nothing. The
576	  `ActivityTable` interface (`Shapes()` and `RenderedWidth()`) is the read-only
577	  face a view hands out for such a guard.
578	
579	**Width cost.** The activity column takes `IconColumnWidth` (2) plus the
580	column gap (2): **4 rendered cells**. Every optional column of a migrated table
581	therefore appears 4 terminal columns later than before, and at 60 columns a
582	required column may give way (Rule 116 allows a whole column to go, never a
583	truncated value). The dot is never the column that gives way. The measured
584	thresholds live with each view: Images and the other OCI tabs in `network.md`
585	(table of before and after), the containers table in `network.md`, the
586	`:agent-usage` agents table in `agent-usage.md`, `:sec` in `scanning.md`.
587	
588	**Known limit.** The header's sort arrow `▲` is also ambiguous-width and is not
589	fitted by `runewidth`: under East Asian width the header line can be one cell
590	off. Only the header, not the rows. It is accepted for now and the test skips
591	line 0.
592	
593	### The selected row in the footer (DEVDESK-140)
594	
595	The footer can say what the selected row is doing, in the same words the
596	activity column's state implies. Every migrated view uses it (DEVDESK-142 to
597	153); the exempt views have no row activity to say (see the guard in
598	`app-shell.md`).
599	
600	**`jobs.ActiveOn(runs, context, target, kinds...) []jobs.Active`**
601	(`internal/jobs/active.go`). The running and queued items on a target in a
602	context: running first, then queued, each group in run order. Target is
603	normalised with `TargetKey` on both sides. No `kinds` keeps every kind. Items
604	are copied without their cancel hook. No match returns nil.
605	
606	**`Status.Detail` and `RowDetail`.** `Status` gains a `Detail RowDetail`
607	(`footer_message.go`); `Status.Text` then becomes the batch progress that
608	follows it. `RowDetail{Glyph, Lead, Target, Tail}` is one sentence; `Target` is
609	a field of its own because only a path is ever shortened.
610	
611	- **`RowStatusLine(detail, progress, width)`** (`jobs_status.go`) joins
612	  them as `<detail> · <progress>` (`rowSeparator`) on at most `width` columns.
613	  Zero detail: the progress alone. No progress: the detail alone.
614	- **Cut order.** A path target shrinks first with `theme.ShortPath`, never
615	  below `minPathCols` (6), then the end of the detail is truncated. An image
616	  reference is not a path (`isPathTarget`: absolute or `~`) and is only
617	  truncated. If fewer than `minDetailCols` (8) columns are left for the detail

  (`MarkBusy`) is `Running` whatever the column says; otherwise the column's

  table never calls it in a test that wants the steady glyph.
- **Padding follows the terminal.** The glyphs `● ○ ◐ ◕ ◉` have ambiguous
  width. lipgloss always counts them as one cell; a terminal in East Asian mode
  draws two. An indicator cell is therefore padded with
  `runewidth.FillRight`, which follows `runewidth.DefaultCondition`.

  line: `padToContent` adds `gap = width - 2 - RenderedWidth()` spaces, computed
  from the column widths. A second measurement with another library would
  disagree on the same glyphs. `TestRule116HoldsUnderEastAsianWidth` pins it.

- **`Shapes()` and `ActivityTable`** (`shape.go`, DEVDESK-142). A cross-view
  guard cannot call a generic `Model[T]` without knowing `T`, so
  `(*Model[T]).Shapes()` returns a fresh `[]ColumnShape` on each call
  (`Title`, `Sizing`, `MinWidth`, and whether the column declares
  `Indicator`, `Less`, `Search`). It reports the declared columns, in order,
  even for an empty table, and mutating the result changes nothing. The
  `ActivityTable` interface (`Shapes()` and `RenderedWidth()`) is the read-only
  face a view hands out for such a guard.

# DEVDESK-341 — Footer: replace the braille spinner by the shared activity dot

Status: plan, awaiting answer to one blocking question (§0). Author: architect.
Inputs: story summary (Plane not readable from this session), `docs/ux/footer-activity-indicator.md`,
user decisions Q1–Q4 (scope = router-driven sites only; progress in text only;
blurred = frozen `●`, no "(paused)"; no dot when the selected row's detail has a glyph).

## 0. Blocking question (to the user)

**The story's own example, `Updating from GitLab...`, is not a router-driven site.**
`internal/ui/forge/explorer/view.go:158` (`Loading <forge> <namespaces>...`) and `:163`
(`Updating from <forge>...`) take their frame from the explorer's own `spinner.Model`
(`explorer/update.go:268`). The explorer is one of the 8 `jobs.FrameMsg` consumers, but
the router frame it receives feeds no status of its own (its clone status has no
`Spinner`). Under Q1 as stated, that line keeps the braille spinner.

- **A — strict Q1.** The explorer only stops writing the router frame into its footer
  (step 2h). `Updating from GitLab...` stays braille until the follow-up story.
- **B — add the two explorer load lines** (step 7, +S). The explorer implements
  `WantsBlink()` while it loads, so the router's 500 ms chain runs. Its `spinner.Model`
  is deleted.
- Recommendation: **B**. It is the story's headline example, it costs little, and it
  also removes the explorer's two-writer race (below). Steps 1–6 do not depend on the
  answer.

# DEVDESK-280 — One width measure for VS16 emoji (datatable, Lip Gloss, viewport)

Status: plan. Author: architect. Base: `main` at `5f76cc16`.
Inputs: story DEVDESK-280 (5 acceptance criteria), `docs/backlog.md` D114, D115 (item 2), D117,
`docs/architecture/ui-components.md`, `.claude/rules/tui-tables.md` (Rules 116, 122, 125).

**Blocking questions: none.** Three choices were taken without asking; they are listed as
hypotheses in §8 (H1–H3) and can be reversed without touching the core of the change.

## 1. What the code does today (measured, not assumed)

`internal/ui/datatable/render.go`:

| Site | Measure | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `fit()` (every cell and every header title) | `runewidth.Truncate`, then `lipgloss…Width(w).MaxWidth(w).Inline(true).Render` | cut by runewidth, padded and re-cut by x/ansi |
| `truncateHead()` (`Column.TruncateHead`) | `runewidth.StringWidth/Truncate/TruncateLeft` | same, through `fit` |
| `rowLine` indicator cell | `runewidth.FillRight` | **deliberate**: follows `runewidth.DefaultCondition.EastAsianWidth` (ambiguous `● ○ ◐`), pinned by `TestRule116HoldsUnderEastAsianWidth` |
| `rebuild()` natural widths (`datatable.go:711,719`) | `lipgloss.Width` = x/ansi | already grapheme |
| `widths.go` sort arrow | `lipgloss.Width` | already grapheme |

Probe of the current `fit` (scratch program, x/ansi v0.11.9, go-runewidth v0.0.31):

| Input | Column | Today | ansi width | Defect |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `✔️` | 1 | `""` | 0 | line one cell short, nothing says there was a value |
| `❤️❤️❤️❤️` | 3 | `"❤️"` | 2 | line one cell short (AC3) |
| `❤️❤️❤️❤️` | 5 | `"❤️❤️"` | 4 | one cell short, marker lost |
| `a❤️x` | 3 | `"a❤️"` | 3 | right width, but no `…`: the cut is silent |
| `x✔️` (head) | 2 | `"x"` | 1 | one cell short |

Why: runewidth counts the cut as fitting (VS16 = 1), lipgloss `Width` pads nothing, then
`MaxWidth` (x/ansi) re-cuts *after* the padding, and a 2-cell cluster that does not fit
leaves a hole. When nothing is cut the width is already right (lipgloss pads by x/ansi):
that is why `TestSelectedRowWithEmojiMeasuresRenderedWidth` is green today.

## 2. Non-functional requirements

- **Correctness (Rule 116):** every rendered table line spans exactly `RenderedWidth()`
  cells measured by `ansi.StringWidth`, VS16 included; a cut never splits a grapheme cluster
  and always shows `…`.
- **East Asian:** no change for the indicator cells (runewidth, by design) nor for the theme
  helpers. x/ansi honours `RUNEWIDTH_EASTASIAN=1` (read at init, `method.go`); a CJK *locale*
  without that variable is honoured by runewidth only. Text cells holding ambiguous-width
  glyphs under a locale-only East Asian terminal were already inconsistent (cut by runewidth,
  padded by x/ansi); after the change they follow x/ansi only. No test covers them today;
  declared, not fixed (§8, R2).
- **`View()` cost (DEVDESK-281 is separate; do not degrade):** measured on a scratch
  benchmark, 8 typical cells at width 20: today 11.1 µs, swap to `ansi.Truncate` alone
  13.4 µs (**+20 %**), swap + printable-ASCII fast path 2.1 µs (**−80 %**). On a 40-row,
  6-column table the plain swap would add about 70 µs per frame (about 8 % of the D114
  868 µs). The fast path is therefore part of this story (step 2), and the step's criterion is
  "`BenchmarkView` no worse than the baseline of step 0". It is not the DEVDESK-281
  optimisation: it only keeps this story from paying for its own change.
- **Exploitability:** no config, no new dependency (`x/ansi` is already a direct dependency;
  `go-runewidth` stays, for the indicator and the theme).

## 4. Design (option A)

All in `internal/ui/datatable/render.go`. Signatures (unexported, package-internal):

```go
// cellWidth is the one width the table sizes, cuts and pads a cell by: the
// grapheme width Lip Gloss and the viewport use (ansi.StringWidth). Printable
// ASCII is measured by its length.
func cellWidth(s string) int

// fit is unchanged in signature and contract: plain text in, exactly `width`
// cells out (measured by ansi.StringWidth), no escape sequence of its own.
func fit(text string, width int, head bool) string

// fitASCII is fit for printable ASCII (0x20..0x7e only): byte slicing, no
// lipgloss call. It must return exactly what fitGraphemes returns for the same
// input (pinned by a test).
func fitASCII(text string, width int, head bool) string

// fitGraphemes is fit for anything else: ansi.Truncate / truncateHead, then the
// existing lipgloss Width(w).MaxWidth(w).Inline(true) render, kept as is so tabs
// and newlines behave exactly as today.
func fitGraphemes(text string, width int, head bool) string

// truncateHead keeps the end (Column.TruncateHead), now on x/ansi. When the
// cut falls inside a 2-cell cluster, that cluster is dropped and a space pads
// after the marker ("… ト"), as runewidth.TruncateLeft does today.
func truncateHead(text string, width int) string

// isPrintableASCII reports whether every byte of s is in 0x20..0x7e.
func isPrintableASCII(s string) bool
```

Reference sketch for `truncateHead` (the coder may write it differently; the tests decide):

```go
total := ansi.StringWidth(text)
if total <= width || width <= 0 { return text }
marker := ansi.StringWidth(truncationMarker)
if width <= marker { return ansi.Truncate(truncationMarker, width, "") }
keep := width - marker
tail := ansi.TruncateLeft(text, total-keep, "")
if ansi.StringWidth(tail) > keep { // a wide cluster straddled the cut
    tail = ansi.TruncateLeft(text, total-keep+1, "")
}
return truncationMarker + strings.Repeat(" ", keep-ansi.StringWidth(tail)) + tail
```

Verified on the scratch probe: `ansi.TruncateLeft("日本語テキスト", 11, "…")` returns
`"…スト"` (5 cells for a budget of 4), hence the correction.

Unchanged on purpose: the indicator branch of `rowLine` (`runewidth.FillRight`), the
natural-width walk in `rebuild()` (already x/ansi through `lipgloss.Width`), `padToContent`,
`spanRuns`, `splitCellRun`.

## 8. Risks, hypotheses, irreversible points

- **R1 — CJK head truncation changes shape.** `ansi.TruncateLeft` keeps a straddling wide
  cluster; without the correction a CJK `TruncateHead` cell would lose its last glyph to
  `MaxWidth` (verified: `"…ス"` instead of `"… ト"`). Covered by
  `TestTruncateHeadKeepsWideClustersWhole`.
- **R2 — East Asian locale without `RUNEWIDTH_EASTASIAN`.** Text cells (not indicator cells)
  with ambiguous glyphs now follow x/ansi only. They were already inconsistent; no test
  covers them; no shipped glyph is affected (§1.3, indicator cells keep runewidth).
- **R3 — `View()` cost.** Gated by step 2 against the step-0 baseline. If the gate fails,
  stop and report rather than loosen it (DEVDESK-281 owns broader optimisation).
- **R4 — Rule 122's rationale weakens.** x/ansi skips escape sequences, so "a styled cell is
  over-measured" is no longer true in this package. The rule stays for the selection-reset and
  rune-slicing reasons (step 4). A future reviewer must not read the change as permission to
  style inside `Cell`.
- **R5 — terminals without mode 2027.** Unchanged and outside the app (renderer measures
  WcWidth). Documented in D128 and D117.
- **Irreversible:** nothing. No schema, no config, no dependency added or removed.

**Hypotheses taken without asking (reversible):**

- **H1** — The theme width helpers (`theme.StringWidth`, `TruncateWidth`, `TruncateTailWidth`)
  stay on runewidth; their VS16 divergence is re-pinned in `internal/ui/theme` and a follow-up

Status: plan. Author: architect. Base: `main` at `5f76cc16`.
Inputs: story DEVDESK-280 (5 acceptance criteria), `docs/backlog.md` D114, D115 (item 2), D117,
`docs/architecture/ui-components.md`, `.claude/rules/tui-tables.md` (Rules 116, 122, 125).

**Blocking questions: none.** Three choices were taken without asking; they are listed as
hypotheses in §8 (H1–H3) and can be reversed without touching the core of the change.

## 1. What the code does today (measured, not assumed)

`internal/ui/datatable/render.go`:

| Site | Measure | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `fit()` (every cell and every header title) | `runewidth.Truncate`, then `lipgloss…Width(w).MaxWidth(w).Inline(true).Render` | cut by runewidth, padded and re-cut by x/ansi |
| `truncateHead()` (`Column.TruncateHead`) | `runewidth.StringWidth/Truncate/TruncateLeft` | same, through `fit` |
| `rowLine` indicator cell | `runewidth.FillRight` | **deliberate**: follows `runewidth.DefaultCondition.EastAsianWidth` (ambiguous `● ○ ◐`), pinned by `TestRule116HoldsUnderEastAsianWidth` |
| `rebuild()` natural widths (`datatable.go:711,719`) | `lipgloss.Width` = x/ansi | already grapheme |
| `widths.go` sort arrow | `lipgloss.Width` | already grapheme |

Probe of the current `fit` (scratch program, x/ansi v0.11.9, go-runewidth v0.0.31):

| Input | Column | Today | ansi width | Defect |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `✔️` | 1 | `""` | 0 | line one cell short, nothing says there was a value |
| `❤️❤️❤️❤️` | 3 | `"❤️"` | 2 | line one cell short (AC3) |
| `❤️❤️❤️❤️` | 5 | `"❤️❤️"` | 4 | one cell short, marker lost |
| `a❤️x` | 3 | `"a❤️"` | 3 | right width, but no `…`: the cut is silent |
| `x✔️` (head) | 2 | `"x"` | 1 | one cell short |

Why: runewidth counts the cut as fitting (VS16 = 1), lipgloss `Width` pads nothing, then
`MaxWidth` (x/ansi) re-cuts *after* the padding, and a 2-cell cluster that does not fit
leaves a hole. When nothing is cut the width is already right (lipgloss pads by x/ansi):
that is why `TestSelectedRowWithEmojiMeasuresRenderedWidth` is green today.

### 1.1 The other measuring sites (checked; out of scope, reasons given)

## 2. Non-functional requirements

  cells measured by `ansi.StringWidth`, VS16 included; a cut never splits a grapheme cluster
  and always shows `…`.

  "`BenchmarkView` no worse than the baseline of step 0". It is not the DEVDESK-281
  optimisation: it only keeps this story from paying for its own change.
- **Exploitability:** no config, no new dependency (`x/ansi` is already a direct dependency;

| | Option | For | Against | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **A** | **The datatable measures, truncates and pads with x/ansi** (`ansi.StringWidth`, `ansi.Truncate`, `ansi.TruncateLeft`), keeping `runewidth.FillRight` for the indicator cell only, plus a printable-ASCII fast path | One measure with Lip Gloss and the viewport, by construction; the library update that fixes VS16 in Lip Gloss fixes the table too; small diff (one file) | `ansi.Truncate` is slower than `runewidth.Truncate` (+20 % on `fit`) → needs the fast path; `ansi.TruncateLeft` keeps a straddling wide cluster (overflow) → `truncateHead` needs a one-cluster correction | **Recommended** |
| B | Keep runewidth, then "bound the truncation": after the cut, re-measure with x/ansi and shrink until it fits, pad by x/ansi | No change of library in the hot path | Two measures stay, the very thing the story removes; a loop on every cut cell; still runewidth's view of what "fits" decides the marker position | Rejected |

| E | Follow the renderer: measure with `WcWidth` until mode 2027 is reported, then grapheme | Matches the terminal exactly | Lip Gloss and the viewport frame always measure grapheme, so the table would then disagree with its own border; needs the `ModeReportMsg` plumbed to every table | Rejected |

## 4. Design (option A)

All in `internal/ui/datatable/render.go`. Signatures (unexported, package-internal):

```go
// cellWidth is the one width the table sizes, cuts and pads a cell by: the
// grapheme width Lip Gloss and the viewport use (ansi.StringWidth). Printable
// ASCII is measured by its length.
func cellWidth(s string) int

// fit is unchanged in signature and contract: plain text in, exactly `width`
// cells out (measured by ansi.StringWidth), no escape sequence of its own.
func fit(text string, width int, head bool) string

// fitASCII is fit for printable ASCII (0x20..0x7e only): byte slicing, no
// lipgloss call. It must return exactly what fitGraphemes returns for the same
// input (pinned by a test).
func fitASCII(text string, width int, head bool) string

// fitGraphemes is fit for anything else: ansi.Truncate / truncateHead, then the
// existing lipgloss Width(w).MaxWidth(w).Inline(true) render, kept as is so tabs
// and newlines behave exactly as today.
func fitGraphemes(text string, width int, head bool) string

// truncateHead keeps the end (Column.TruncateHead), now on x/ansi. When the
// cut falls inside a 2-cell cluster, that cluster is dropped and a space pads
// after the marker ("… ト"), as runewidth.TruncateLeft does today.
func truncateHead(text string, width int) string

// isPrintableASCII reports whether every byte of s is in 0x20..0x7e.
func isPrintableASCII(s string) bool
```

Reference sketch for `truncateHead` (the coder may write it differently; the tests decide):

```go
total := ansi.StringWidth(text)
if total <= width || width <= 0 { return text }
marker := ansi.StringWidth(truncationMarker)
if width <= marker { return ansi.Truncate(truncationMarker, width, "") }
keep := width - marker
tail := ansi.TruncateLeft(text, total-keep, "")
if ansi.StringWidth(tail) > keep { // a wide cluster straddled the cut
    tail = ansi.TruncateLeft(text, total-keep+1, "")
}
return truncationMarker + strings.Repeat(" ", keep-ansi.StringWidth(tail)) + tail
```

Verified on the scratch probe: `ansi.TruncateLeft("日本語テキスト", 11, "…")` returns
`"…スト"` (5 cells for a budget of 4), hence the correction.

```go
func cellWidth(s string) int

func truncateHead(text string, width int) string

func isPrintableASCII(s string) bool
```

```go
total := ansi.StringWidth(text)
if total <= width || width <= 0 { return text }
marker := ansi.StringWidth(truncationMarker)
if width <= marker { return ansi.Truncate(truncationMarker, width, "") }
keep := width - marker
tail := ansi.TruncateLeft(text, total-keep, "")
if ansi.StringWidth(tail) > keep { // a wide cluster straddled the cut

}
return truncationMarker + strings.Repeat(" ", keep-ansi.StringWidth(tail)) + tail
```

Status: plan. Author: architect. Base: `main` at `5f76cc16`.
Inputs: story DEVDESK-280 (5 acceptance criteria), `docs/backlog.md` D114, D115 (item 2), D117,
`docs/architecture/ui-components.md`, `.claude/rules/tui-tables.md` (Rules 116, 122, 125).

hypotheses in §8 (H1–H3) and can be reversed without touching the core of the change.

## 1. What the code does today (measured, not assumed)

`internal/ui/datatable/render.go`:

| Site | Measure | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `fit()` (every cell and every header title) | `runewidth.Truncate`, then `lipgloss…Width(w).MaxWidth(w).Inline(true).Render` | cut by runewidth, padded and re-cut by x/ansi |
| `truncateHead()` (`Column.TruncateHead`) | `runewidth.StringWidth/Truncate/TruncateLeft` | same, through `fit` |
| `rowLine` indicator cell | `runewidth.FillRight` | **deliberate**: follows `runewidth.DefaultCondition.EastAsianWidth` (ambiguous `● ○ ◐`), pinned by `TestRule116HoldsUnderEastAsianWidth` |
| `rebuild()` natural widths (`datatable.go:711,719`) | `lipgloss.Width` = x/ansi | already grapheme |
| `widths.go` sort arrow | `lipgloss.Width` | already grapheme |

Probe of the current `fit` (scratch program, x/ansi v0.11.9, go-runewidth v0.0.31):

| Input | Column | Today | ansi width | Defect |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `✔️` | 1 | `""` | 0 | line one cell short, nothing says there was a value |
| `❤️❤️❤️❤️` | 3 | `"❤️"` | 2 | line one cell short (AC3) |
| `❤️❤️❤️❤️` | 5 | `"❤️❤️"` | 4 | one cell short, marker lost |
| `a❤️x` | 3 | `"a❤️"` | 3 | right width, but no `…`: the cut is silent |
| `x✔️` (head) | 2 | `"x"` | 1 | one cell short |

Why: runewidth counts the cut as fitting (VS16 = 1), lipgloss `Width` pads nothing, then
`MaxWidth` (x/ansi) re-cuts *after* the padding, and a 2-cell cluster that does not fit
leaves a hole. When nothing is cut the width is already right (lipgloss pads by x/ansi):
that is why `TestSelectedRowWithEmojiMeasuresRenderedWidth` is green today.

### 1.1 The other measuring sites (checked; out of scope, reasons given)

- **The Bubble Tea v2 renderer** (`cursed_renderer.go`, ultraviolet `buffer.go:617`) measures
  with `ansi.WcWidth` (VS16 = 1) **by default**, and switches to `ansi.GraphemeWidth` only when
  the terminal answers mode 2027 (`tea.go:822`). This is not ours to change, and it does not
  depend on the datatable: Lip Gloss and the viewport border already pad by grapheme width, so
  on a terminal without 2027 a line holding a VS16 emoji can show its right border one cell

  before it, it disagreed with both.
- **`theme.StringWidth`, `TruncateWidth`, `TruncateTailWidth`, `gauge.go`, `path.go`,
  `components/footer_message.go`** (14 non-test call sites): runewidth on purpose. They follow

### 1.2 Tests that pin go-runewidth today

### 1.3 Regression scan of every glyph the app ships

All 697 distinct non-ASCII string literals in non-test `internal/**/*.go` (Nerd Font icons,

**one** divergence, an escape string inside a comment (`render.go:23`). No icon, Nerd Font

## 2. Non-functional requirements

  "`BenchmarkView` no worse than the baseline of step 0". It is not the DEVDESK-281
  optimisation: it only keeps this story from paying for its own change.
- **Exploitability:** no config, no new dependency (`x/ansi` is already a direct dependency;

## 3. Options

| | Option | For | Against | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **A** | **The datatable measures, truncates and pads with x/ansi** (`ansi.StringWidth`, `ansi.Truncate`, `ansi.TruncateLeft`), keeping `runewidth.FillRight` for the indicator cell only, plus a printable-ASCII fast path | One measure with Lip Gloss and the viewport, by construction; the library update that fixes VS16 in Lip Gloss fixes the table too; small diff (one file) | `ansi.Truncate` is slower than `runewidth.Truncate` (+20 % on `fit`) → needs the fast path; `ansi.TruncateLeft` keeps a straddling wide cluster (overflow) → `truncateHead` needs a one-cluster correction | **Recommended** |
| B | Keep runewidth, then "bound the truncation": after the cut, re-measure with x/ansi and shrink until it fits, pad by x/ansi | No change of library in the hot path | Two measures stay, the very thing the story removes; a loop on every cut cell; still runewidth's view of what "fits" decides the marker position | Rejected |

| E | Follow the renderer: measure with `WcWidth` until mode 2027 is reported, then grapheme | Matches the terminal exactly | Lip Gloss and the viewport frame always measure grapheme, so the table would then disagree with its own border; needs the `ModeReportMsg` plumbed to every table | Rejected |

## 4. Design (option A)

All in `internal/ui/datatable/render.go`. Signatures (unexported, package-internal):

```go
// cellWidth is the one width the table sizes, cuts and pads a cell by: the
// grapheme width Lip Gloss and the viewport use (ansi.StringWidth). Printable
// ASCII is measured by its length.
func cellWidth(s string) int

// fit is unchanged in signature and contract: plain text in, exactly `width`
// cells out (measured by ansi.StringWidth), no escape sequence of its own.
func fit(text string, width int, head bool) string

// fitASCII is fit for printable ASCII (0x20..0x7e only): byte slicing, no
// lipgloss call. It must return exactly what fitGraphemes returns for the same
// input (pinned by a test).
func fitASCII(text string, width int, head bool) string

// fitGraphemes is fit for anything else: ansi.Truncate / truncateHead, then the
// existing lipgloss Width(w).MaxWidth(w).Inline(true) render, kept as is so tabs
// and newlines behave exactly as today.
func fitGraphemes(text string, width int, head bool) string

// truncateHead keeps the end (Column.TruncateHead), now on x/ansi. When the
// cut falls inside a 2-cell cluster, that cluster is dropped and a space pads
// after the marker ("… ト"), as runewidth.TruncateLeft does today.
func truncateHead(text string, width int) string

// isPrintableASCII reports whether every byte of s is in 0x20..0x7e.
func isPrintableASCII(s string) bool
```

Reference sketch for `truncateHead` (the coder may write it differently; the tests decide):

```go
total := ansi.StringWidth(text)
if total <= width || width <= 0 { return text }
marker := ansi.StringWidth(truncationMarker)
if width <= marker { return ansi.Truncate(truncationMarker, width, "") }
keep := width - marker
tail := ansi.TruncateLeft(text, total-keep, "")
if ansi.StringWidth(tail) > keep { // a wide cluster straddled the cut
    tail = ansi.TruncateLeft(text, total-keep+1, "")
}
return truncationMarker + strings.Repeat(" ", keep-ansi.StringWidth(tail)) + tail
```

then `go test $T -count=2`, then `go test ./internal/ui/... -count=1` (every view that builds a
table: containers, ws, sec, oci, net, jobs, agent usage).

`TestSelectedRowWithEmojiMeasuresRenderedWidth`, `TestDatatableWidthAgreesWithTheGraphemeWidth`
(still in place until step 3) and the whole `internal/ui/...` suite are green.

### Step 2 — printable-ASCII fast path (S; after step 1)

Tests first, `internal/ui/datatable/width_test.go`:

1. **`TestTheASCIIFastPathMatchesTheGraphemePath`**: for a corpus of printable-ASCII strings
   (empty, 1 char, `"192.168.1.240"`, `"registry.example.com/team/app:1.2.3"`, leading and
   trailing spaces, punctuation), widths 1..40, head false and true:
   `fitASCII(s, w, h) == fitGraphemes(s, w, h)` **byte for byte**. (Checked on the scratch
   probe for the tail cut: 0 differences over 8 strings × 25 widths.)
2. **`TestIsPrintableASCII`**: `"abc"` → true; `"a\tb"`, `"a\nb"`, `"\x1b[m"`, `"é"`, `"✔️"`,
   `"\x7f"` → false.
3. **`TestCellWidthMatchesAnsiOnASCII`**: `cellWidth(s) == ansi.StringWidth(s)` on the corpus.

Code, `render.go`: `fit` dispatches on `isPrintableASCII(text) && width > 0` to `fitASCII`
(tail: `text[:width-1] + truncationMarker` when `len(text) > width`, else pad with spaces;
head: `truncationMarker + text[len(text)-(width-1):]`, width 1 → the marker alone), else
`fitGraphemes`. `cellWidth` returns `len(s)` on printable ASCII, else `ansi.StringWidth(s)`.

**Run:** the three tests, then
`go test $T -run '^$' -bench 'BenchmarkFit|BenchmarkView' -benchmem -count=7`.

**Done when:** tests green; `BenchmarkView` median ≤ the step-0 median (5 % noise allowance,
stated in the PR with both figures); `BenchmarkFit/vs16` and `/cjk` may be slower than step 0
(they were wrong before) and are reported, not gated.

## 6. Order and parallelism

```
0 ──► 1 ──► 2 ──┐
        └─► 3 ──┴─► 4 ──► 5
```

Steps 2 and 3 can run in parallel after 1 (different files except `width_test.go`: step 3
removes `agreedWidths`, step 2 adds tests; merge order 2 then 3, or one coder for both).
One PR for the story; a step is a commit.

## 7. Acceptance criteria → tests

| AC | Test |
|---|---|
| 1 `✔️` same width | `TestDatatableMeasuresVS16LikeAnsi` |
| 2 `a❤️x` same width | `TestDatatableMeasuresVS16LikeAnsi` |
| 3 truncated VS16 column exactly its width, no split | `REDACTED`, `TestAVS16CutNeverSplitsACluster`, `FuzzFitSpansTheColumn` |
| 4 divergence test inverted | `REDACTED` deleted, replaced by `TestDatatableMeasuresVS16LikeAnsi` (fails on divergence) |
| 5 width-1 emoji, CJK, ZWJ, flags stay green | `TestTheTableFillsTheViewportAtThreeWidths` (kept, extended), `TestThemeStringWidthAgreesWithTheGraphemeWidth` (moved), `TestTruncateHeadKeepsWideClustersWhole`, `TestRule116HoldsUnderEastAsianWidth`, `TestSelectedRowWithEmojiMeasuresRenderedWidth` |

## 8. Risks, hypotheses, irreversible points

- **R1 — CJK head truncation changes shape.** `ansi.TruncateLeft` keeps a straddling wide
  cluster; without the correction a CJK `TruncateHead` cell would lose its last glyph to
  `MaxWidth` (verified: `"…ス"` instead of `"… ト"`). Covered by
  `TestTruncateHeadKeepsWideClustersWhole`.
- **R2 — East Asian locale without `RUNEWIDTH_EASTASIAN`.** Text cells (not indicator cells)
  with ambiguous glyphs now follow x/ansi only. They were already inconsistent; no test
  covers them; no shipped glyph is affected (§1.3, indicator cells keep runewidth).
- **R3 — `View()` cost.** Gated by step 2 against the step-0 baseline. If the gate fails,
  stop and report rather than loosen it (DEVDESK-281 owns broader optimisation).
- **R4 — Rule 122's rationale weakens.** x/ansi skips escape sequences, so "a styled cell is
  over-measured" is no longer true in this package. The rule stays for the selection-reset and
  rune-slicing reasons (step 4). A future reviewer must not read the change as permission to
  style inside `Cell`.
- **R5 — terminals without mode 2027.** Unchanged and outside the app (renderer measures
  WcWidth). Documented in D128 and D117.
- **Irreversible:** nothing. No schema, no config, no dependency added or removed.

**Hypotheses taken without asking (reversible):**

- **H1** — The theme width helpers (`theme.StringWidth`, `TruncateWidth`, `TruncateTailWidth`)
  stay on runewidth; their VS16 divergence is re-pinned in `internal/ui/theme` and a follow-up
  story is proposed. Reason: they carry the East Asian handling of the footer, and the story
  names the datatable, Lip Gloss and the viewport only.
- **H2** — The rule files (`tui-tables.md` Rules 116 and 122) are corrected for facts only;
  no rule is added, removed or loosened.
- **H3** — The printable-ASCII fast path ships with this story, because without it the change
  costs about +20 % on `fit` (+8 % of a frame). It is byte-identical to the general path
  (tested) and local to `render.go`.

## 9. Follow-ups to file (not in this story)

1. **Theme width helpers on one measure** (`theme.StringWidth`, `TruncateWidth`,
   `TruncateTailWidth`, `components/footer_message.go`): decide how East Asian ambiguous width
   is honoured if they move to x/ansi (`RUNEWIDTH_EASTASIAN` only, or a wrapper). Unpins
   `TestThemeStringWidthVS16IsAKnownDivergence`.
2. **Viewer soft wrap by width, not runes** (`internal/ui/viewer/lines.go: wrapTokens`): CJK
   and VS16 lines wrap at the wrong column and can split a cluster.

## 10. Effort

S–M overall: step 0 XS, step 1 S (one file of code, about six tests), step 2 S, step 3 S,
step 4 S, step 5 XS. Hypothesis behind it: no view needs a change (every view goes through
`fit`; §1.3 shows no shipped glyph changes width).

An escape sequence inside a `Cell` (forbidden by Rule 122) is walked as text, as runewidth
does today: `ESC` is a zero-width cluster and `[38;2;…m` counts one cell per byte. This is
deliberate and kept: it is the premise of Rule 122 ("a styled cell is over-measured and cut
mid-escape"), so `cellWidth` is defined as **the sum of the walk's cluster widths**, not as a
call to `ansi.StringWidth` (which skips escapes). On plain text the two are equal, and the
tests pin that equality; on styled text the table's measure over-counts, as before.

## DEVDESK-280 : compte rendu de l'architecte

Le plan est écrit dans `/home/anthoni/projects/workspace-entire/anthnel/devdesk/.claude/plans/DEVDESK-280-plan.md`. C'est le seul fichier modifié. Les sondes et le benchmark ont tourné dans un programme jetable du scratchpad, pas dans le dépôt.

**Questions bloquantes : aucune.** J'ai tranché trois points sans demander, tous réversibles (voir la fin).

### Choix retenu
Le datatable mesure, coupe et complète chaque cellule par grappes de graphèmes (en anglais, *grapheme clusters*). Il parcourt la chaîne avec `ansi.FirstGraphemeCluster(s, ansi.GraphemeWidth)`, la fonction dont `ansi.StringWidth` additionne les résultats : ses largeurs sont donc celles de Lip Gloss et du viewport.
- **Ce qui ne change pas :**
  - `runewidth.FillRight` reste pour la cellule indicateur. Il gère la largeur ambiguë des écrans est-asiatiques, et ses glyphes font une seule rune, donc jamais de VS16.
  - Le rendu lipgloss final ne bouge pas.
- **Raccourci pour l'ASCII imprimable :** le résultat est identique octet pour octet au chemin général (vérifié).

### Ce que j'ai constaté (les choix en découlent)
- **Le `fit` actuel** coupe avec runewidth puis repasse par `MaxWidth`, qui mesure avec x/ansi. Résultat :
  - `❤️❤️❤️❤️` dans 3 cellules en fait 2 ;
  - `✔️` dans 1 cellule en fait 0 ;
  - `a❤️x` coupé n'affiche pas `…` ;
  - les keycaps `1️⃣2️⃣3️⃣` débordent de 2 cellules.
- **x/ansi v0.11.9 n'est pas cohérent avec lui-même :** `ansi.Truncate` laisse passer les keycaps en entier, et `ansi.TruncateLeft` garde une grappe large à cheval sur la coupe (`"…スト"` pour 4 cellules). Aucune de ces deux fonctions ne peut servir de coupe. Le prototype qui parcourt les grappes passe 20 017 chaînes (dont 20 000 aléatoires), en largeurs 1 à 12 et dans les deux sens. La version avec `ansi.Truncate` échoue sur le même corpus.
- **Le moteur de rendu de Bubble Tea v2** mesure en `WcWidth`, où un VS16 compte 1, tant que le terminal ne répond pas au mode 2027. Ce point échappe à l'application et c'est déjà la vérification manuelle de D117. Après le changement, le tableau est au moins d'accord avec son cadre Lip Gloss.
- **Les 697 chaînes non ASCII du code**, dont les icônes Nerd Font et les indicateurs, ont la même largeur dans les deux bibliothèques. Le changement ne touche donc que les données affichées dans les cellules.
- **Le parcours compte une séquence d'échappement comme du texte**, comme runewidth. Le motif de la Rule 122 reste donc vrai, et un test le fige.

### Alternatives écartées
- **A′ (`ansi.Truncate` et `ansi.TruncateLeft`) :** débordent sur les keycaps et sur le CJK.
- **B (borner la coupe runewidth) :** garde deux mesures.
- **C (calcul maison runewidth + VS16) :** réimplémente une partie d'UAX 29 dans l'application.
- **D (passer aussi les helpers `theme.*` sur x/ansi) :** casse la gestion est-asiatique du footer, et c'est hors périmètre.
- **E (suivre la méthode négociée par le terminal) :** le cadre Lip Gloss mesure toujours en graphèmes, le tableau serait alors en désaccord avec sa propre bordure.

### Étapes
- **Étape 0 (XS) :** référence de performance. `BenchmarkFit` et `BenchmarkView` dans `datatable/bench_test.go`.
- **Étape 1 (S) :** `cellWidth`, `truncateTail` et `truncateHead` parcourent les grappes. Tests écrits avant le code :
  - `TestDatatableMeasuresVS16LikeAnsi` (remplace `REDACTED`) ;
  - `TestAVS16CutNeverSplitsACluster` ;
  - `REDACTED` ;
  - `TestTruncateHeadKeepsWideClustersWhole` (garde la forme CJK actuelle `"… ト"`) ;
  - `FuzzFitSpansTheColumn` ;
  - garde-fou `TestDatatableMeasuresWithOneLibrary` : seul `runewidth.FillRight` reste autorisé ;
  - `TestTheTableFillsTheViewportAtThreeWidths` est modifié : VS16 ajoutés, assertion runewidth retirée.
- **Étape 2 (S) :** raccourci ASCII, avec `TestTheASCIIFastPathMatchesTheGraphemePath`, `TestIsPrintableASCII` et `TestCellWidthMatchesAnsiOnPlainText`. Critère : la médiane de `BenchmarkView` ne dépasse pas celle de l'étape 0 (marge de 5 %).
- **Étape 3 (S, en parallèle de l'étape 2) :**
  - le test d'accord runewidth/ansi part dans `theme/text_test.go` ;
  - un nouveau test y fige l'écart VS16 de `theme.StringWidth` : `TestThemeStringWidthVS16IsAKnownDivergence` ;
  - `TestRunewidthMisreads…` est réécrit en `TestTheTableCutMisreadsStyledTextWhichIsWhyCellIsPlain`.
- **Étape 4 (S) :** documentation.
- **Étape 5 (XS) :** `mise run check` et `go test ./internal/ui/datatable -count=2`, puis vérification manuelle par l'utilisateur, avec et sans mode 2027.

Commande ciblée :
`go test ./internal/ui/datatable -run 'VS16|Truncat|Fills|Fit|OneLibrary|EastAsian|Emoji|Measure' -count=1`
puis `go test ./internal/ui/... -count=1`.

### Fichiers touchés
- **Code :** `internal/ui/datatable/render.go` ; commentaire seulement dans `datatable.go`.

## DEVDESK-280 : compte rendu de l'architecte

Le plan est écrit dans `/home/anthoni/projects/workspace-entire/anthnel/devdesk/.claude/plans/DEVDESK-280-plan.md`. C'est le seul fichier modifié. Les sondes et le benchmark ont tourné dans un programme jetable du scratchpad, pas dans le dépôt.

**Questions bloquantes : aucune.** J'ai tranché trois points sans demander, tous réversibles (voir la fin).

### Choix retenu
Le datatable mesure, coupe et complète chaque cellule par grappes de graphèmes (en anglais, *grapheme clusters*). Il parcourt la chaîne avec `ansi.FirstGraphemeCluster(s, ansi.GraphemeWidth)`, la fonction dont `ansi.StringWidth` additionne les résultats : ses largeurs sont donc celles de Lip Gloss et du viewport.
- **Ce qui ne change pas :**
  - `runewidth.FillRight` reste pour la cellule indicateur. Il gère la largeur ambiguë des écrans est-asiatiques, et ses glyphes font une seule rune, donc jamais de VS16.
  - Le rendu lipgloss final ne bouge pas.
- **Raccourci pour l'ASCII imprimable :** le résultat est identique octet pour octet au chemin général (vérifié).

### Ce que j'ai constaté (les choix en découlent)
- **Le `fit` actuel** coupe avec runewidth puis repasse par `MaxWidth`, qui mesure avec x/ansi. Résultat :
  - `❤️❤️❤️❤️` dans 3 cellules en fait 2 ;
  - `✔️` dans 1 cellule en fait 0 ;
  - `a❤️x` coupé n'affiche pas `…` ;
  - les keycaps `1️⃣2️⃣3️⃣` débordent de 2 cellules.
- **x/ansi v0.11.9 n'est pas cohérent avec lui-même :** `ansi.Truncate` laisse passer les keycaps en entier, et `ansi.TruncateLeft` garde une grappe large à cheval sur la coupe (`"…スト"` pour 4 cellules). Aucune de ces deux fonctions ne peut servir de coupe. Le prototype qui parcourt les grappes passe 20 017 chaînes (dont 20 000 aléatoires), en largeurs 1 à 12 et dans les deux sens. La version avec `ansi.Truncate` échoue sur le même corpus.
- **Le moteur de rendu de Bubble Tea v2** mesure en `WcWidth`, où un VS16 compte 1, tant que le terminal ne répond pas au mode 2027. Ce point échappe à l'application et c'est déjà la vérification manuelle de D117. Après le changement, le tableau est au moins d'accord avec son cadre Lip Gloss.
- **Les 697 chaînes non ASCII du code**, dont les icônes Nerd Font et les indicateurs, ont la même largeur dans les deux bibliothèques. Le changement ne touche donc que les données affichées dans les cellules.
- **Le parcours compte une séquence d'échappement comme du texte**, comme runewidth. Le motif de la Rule 122 reste donc vrai, et un test le fige.

### Alternatives écartées
- **A′ (`ansi.Truncate` et `ansi.TruncateLeft`) :** débordent sur les keycaps et sur le CJK.
- **B (borner la coupe runewidth) :** garde deux mesures.
- **C (calcul maison runewidth + VS16) :** réimplémente une partie d'UAX 29 dans l'application.
- **D (passer aussi les helpers `theme.*` sur x/ansi) :** casse la gestion est-asiatique du footer, et c'est hors périmètre.
- **E (suivre la méthode négociée par le terminal) :** le cadre Lip Gloss mesure toujours en graphèmes, le tableau serait alors en désaccord avec sa propre bordure.

  - `TestDatatableMeasuresVS16LikeAnsi` (remplace `REDACTED`) ;
  - `TestAVS16CutNeverSplitsACluster` ;
